en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Two Triplets on the Internal (Ajjhattattikadvaya).
A non-visible, non-reactive, non-internal state is a condition for a non-visible, non-reactive, internal state by way of object-condition.
(Abbreviated. There are six [conditions] in the case of the object, six in the case of predominance, and six in the cases of prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.
A non-visible, non-reactive, non-external state is [a condition] for a non-visible, non-reactive, external state...
Conditioned by object-condition. (Abbreviated. Six [conditions] for object, six for predominance, six for prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and not internal as its object, there arises a state that is non-visible, non-reacting, and internal as its object, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three for root ... pe ... three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and not having an external object, there arises a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and having an external object, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. There are three [answers] for root; ... pe ... three for non-disappearance.

(The section on co-nascence, the section on conditions, the section on dependence, the section on association, the section on conjunction, and the section on inquiry should also be expanded in detail.)
